title: The Azumi, seafarers of northern Kyushu, from the 3rd century
summary: The Azumi were a seafaring clan of northern Kyushu whose night navigation made them useful to the Yamato court from the 3rd century and, in effect, its navy. They are said to have come to control the sea routes of the Inland Sea and to have settled in Settsu, near Osaka. A tradition has some of them going inland to the Azumi basin in Nagano; that leg rests on tourism and popular pages and is drawn as a guess.

events.label: Shikanoshima, where the Azumi are honoured
events.text: A shrine on the island's Genkai Bay side is dedicated to Azumi no Isora, with stones for sea turtles and over a thousand deer antlers. Another shrine in Fukuoka is called the Azumi's ancestral shrine. The article makes them the effective navy of Yamato from the 3rd to early 5th century.

events.label: The Azumi basin
events.doubt: The two sources the article gives for the move inland are a tourism page and a 2011 Yahoo Voices article.
events.text: Azumino, in Nagano, keeps the clan's name. The article says some Azumi settled here, and folklore recorded about a thousand years ago speaks of the settlement.
